newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan welcomes first Peru hostage to return home.
newsitem.headline: Japan welcomes first Peru hostage to return home.

text.p: The first Japanese hostage rescued from Marxist rebels in Lima, Peru, returned home on Friday after four months in captivity.

Shigeru Taki, 59, president of National Peruana S.A., Matsushita Electric Industrial Co's Peru branch, arrived at Kansai International Airport in the central commercial city of Osaka shortly after 6 p.m (0900 gmt).
"The first thing I want to do is go home, stretch and get some rest," said Taki, who was riding in a wheelchair and accompanied by his wife Tetsuyo, two tearful daughters and a Matsushita executive.

Taki was one of the 71 hostages, including 24 Japanese, rescued on Wednesday in the fiery military strike which ended a 18-week siege at the Japanese ambassador's home by Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels.
Taki, one of Matsushita's Latin America experts and a veteran of more than a decade in the region, said he would return to Peru after a brief vacation.
